ab_calgary.blurb: Climbing around Calgary, Alberta, is almost entirely bouldering, with a single sport route among the climbs. Problems run from V0 up to V10, with the heaviest concentration between V4 and V7 and a solid number of easier ones beneath. Millennium Park, in the city, holds the most climbs. Its three boulders, roughly 3.6 to 4.25 metres tall, were installed and opened in summer 2023, and its problems were set by Canadian climbers. Bearspaw Bluffs Bouldering and Split Rock Bouldering are smaller sub-areas, and a handful of single boulders are scattered elsewhere around the region.

az_atlantis.blurb: Atlantis is a sport-focused area in Queen Creek Canyon, above the town of Superior and about an hour east of Phoenix. It sits in a deep cleft just past the big tunnel on the drive from Superior toward Globe. The rock in Queen Creek Canyon is volcanic tuff, and at Atlantis the holds tend to be small edges rather than the pockets found at many other Queen Creek areas. Most climbs are sport, with a good number of trad lines and a few boulders, and grades run from 5.6 to 5.13 with the largest groups at 5.10 and 5.11. It is one of the few areas near Phoenix that can be climbed in summer, by starting early and following the shade from one side of the canyon to the other. Atlantis South Side holds the most climbs, followed by Atlantis North Side, The Funny Farm and Kitty Pool.

az_hairpin_turn_area.blurb: Hairpin Turn Area is on Mount Lemmon in the Santa Catalina Mountains, along the lower stretch of the highway in a Sonoran Desert setting of saguaro cactus. Its elevation is close to Tucson's, so climbing works in late fall, winter and early spring. The drive and the approaches, roughly 10 to 25 minutes, are easy. Most climbs are sport, with a good number of trad lines and some that mix bolts with gear, and grades run from the 5.7s to 5.12 with most at 5.10 and 5.11. The rock quality is poor. Walls differ in sun: Backhand Wall faces north and gets little or no sun, Forehand Wall and Left Hand Wall face east, and Tweener Wall faces south. Pinhead Wall, Right Hand Wall and Hairpin, and Left Hand Wall hold the most climbs.

ca_main_formation.blurb: The Main Formation is the central cluster of cliffs at Lover's Leap, in the Highway 50 corridor of the Lake Tahoe area near Strawberry. It divides into four walls: West Wall, Main Wall, Central Wall and East Wall. The cliff at the Leap is mostly vertical granite split by hundreds of cracks and crossed by thousands of horizontal dikes, which give rests and plenty of holds and keep many grades moderate. The Main Wall is the tallest formation there, at about 500 feet. Climbing on the Main Formation is overwhelmingly trad with a few sport routes, and grades run from 5.7 to 5.12, centered on 5.9 and 5.10. East Wall and Main Wall hold the most climbs.

ca_mount_diablo_state_park.blurb: Mount Diablo State Park lies southeast of Walnut Creek and northeast of Danville, in the East Bay of the San Francisco Bay Area. Climbing here is varied: sport routes make up the most, followed by top-rope and trad, with a little bouldering away from the main crags. Most of the rock is soft sandstone that suits smearing and edging. Grades are mostly 5.10 and 5.11, with a smaller group of moderates and some 5.12. Pine Canyon offers multi-pitch adventure climbing, both sport and trad, on moderate routes, with long approaches and some route-finding; it is most comfortable on summer mornings and evenings and from November through May. Pine Canyon and Boy Scout Rocks hold the most climbs.
